chapter: The Washingtonians, Bechet and drum style
title: The band as family and being the last original: 'I was there'
summary: Greer reminisces that the original band is gone, and says 'I was there' when challenged by smart people; Gregory's club.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Beautiful. Beautiful. Beautiful man. Bechet was -- everybody loved him. Even Duke loved him. He was just a funloving man. He lived. He lived. He was beautiful. In fact, all the whole band was beautiful. A bunch of guys that could play, stars, and they was a family. They were a family, please believe me. It was one for all and all for one and Duke was right in=the middle of them. I remember this, reminisce
all of them are gone now, I'm the only one around of the originals, and I don't generally talk about it, bring back too many memories, you know.

And I'm not a sentimentalist. But I recall the many pleasant moments we had together. That's why when a guy, somebody come up to me, I was playing a school, a college and a guy say, so and so and so and so, and some guy, smart guy, uh, only thing I say to him, 'I was there.' That's all I had to say. 'I was there, pal.' You just quoting something to me maybe you read. I was there.' That take care of all that. I was there. That's right.
I remember when I stopped -- I was playing -- I went down to a club in New York here, 62nd Street and 1st Avenue, called Gregory's -- you never been there.
Yeah, I used to come in there and see you all the time.

I used to run across that all the time, you know. Run across different -- you know, white people curious all the time, and I get a kick out of it, laugh, you know. They ask me different things. You know, especially school kids. I tell them something, they brush them off, not impolite, I say, Well some friends of mine are leaving for Chicago. I got to go and tell them goodnight. That's the whiskbroom. I call it the whiskbroom, and they're happy. That's right.
